messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 ALERT: Dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-87f3) reporting >95% request failures for tenant 'NordicBank' (VPC). Errors: TCP connection reset + model timeout. Impact: customer-facing API errors and increased latency. Page routed to #incidents and @alice oncall. first_seen=1747008100

alice oncall: I’m on it — joining bridge now. Can someone grab context: which region and which model?

ben sres: Region eu-north-1, Dedicated pool dp-87f3 backed by 4xA100s. Model is llama-13b-q4f (quantized). Seeing repeated `connection reset by peer` from workers and `kv cache OOM` spikes in logs.

carla acct-mgr: Notifying account team. NordicBank has an active Dedicated contract and strict SLA. They're on a maintenance window later today but this is outside that. I'll open a critical support case and ping their security contact.

daniel se: Adding context from onboarding: NordicBank uses private VPC peering and has flow logs showing intermittent spikes. Could be TCP churn from their side, but stack trace shows workers dropping while accepting connections.

erin eng-runtime: On the runtime side I'm seeing repeated worker restarts tied to CUDA OOM followed by soft-failover attempts. Example snippet from node logs: ```2024-11-02T12:12:01Z worker-3 ERROR cudaOutOfMemory: alloc failed for KV cache page=8192``` Might be a quantization regression with sequence length on their RLHF prompts.

ben sres: Immediate mitigations: 1) mark pool dp-87f3 as draining to stop new sessions, 2) spin up ephemeral fallback pool (hosted) and route all NordicBank traffic there, 3) throttle very large seq requests from that tenant, 4) collect full crash dumps. I'll run the commands.

alice oncall: Do the drain and route now. Carla, prepare a short customer note: "We detected degraded availability for your dedicated endpoint; we’re failing over to a temporary capacity while we investigate." Keep it high-level.

ben sres: Running: ```./infractl pool drain --id dp-87f3 --reason "OOM storm" && ./infractl route override --tenant NordicBank --to hosted-fallback-eu --ttl 3600```

ops-bot: pool dp-87f3 state changed -> DRAINING

ops-bot: route override applied for tenant NordicBank -> hosted-fallback-eu (ttl=3600)

ben sres: Fallback routing applied. Observed error rate drop from 96% -> 12% over the last 3 minutes. Latency spike persists for in-flight sessions.

carla acct-mgr: Sent provisional note to NordicBank security and platform leads. They replied: "Acknowledged. Please confirm any potential data exposure." They want an exec update in 30m.

frank security: From initial S3/audit checks there's no sign of data exfil. VPC flow logs show connection resets but not unusual egress. We'll continue forensically collecting dump and netflow.

alice oncall: Good. Next: can we isolate root cause to their tenant traffic shape vs runtime bug? Erin/Ben, can you reproduce locally with large seq prompts? If it's tenant load, implement temporary rate limit.

erin eng-runtime: I can repro partial OOM by replaying their top 10 longest prompts (sanitized) in a staging pool. Looks like sequence len > 12k tok triggers kv cache blowout on quantized kernel path. Suspect an edge-case quant path at high seq lengths.

ben sres: For safety, I've inserted a temporary tenant policy: `max_input_tokens=8192` for NordicBank at the gateway. Applied via: ```./gwctl set-tenant-limit --tenant NordicBank --max-tokens 8192```

ops-bot: tenant limit updated for NordicBank: max_input_tokens=8192

ben sres: Error rate for fallback pool now down to 2%. We should keep fallback and drain in place until we patch/rollback the quant kernel.

alice oncall: We're stabilised. Next steps for post-incident: 1) Capture RCA draft, 2) Prepare exec update for NordicBank, 3) Propose SLA credit and timeline for permanent fix, 4) Postmortem runbook and kernel rollback. Carla, can you coordinate customer comms and confirm they want a live bridge?

carla acct-mgr: They want a 1:1 bridge now with execs. Scheduling 15-min sync. I'll also put together the initial exec summary: short timeline, current status, next actions, and proposed goodwill credit.

ben sres: For the engineering RCA: root cause hypothesis — quantized kernel path mishandles extreme KV cache growth at seq > ~10k, leading to CUDA alloc failures and worker restarts. Repro steps: replay sanitized prompt X -> OOM in staging with same q4f config. Fix options: revert to prior kernel build (v1.4.2) or add aggressive prefork/kv-eviction. I recommend rollback to v1.4.2 for immediate mitigation.

erin eng-runtime: Patch ready: either 1) revert kernel as Ben suggests, or 2) land kv-eviction RFC which will take ~5 business days. I can prepare a rollback patch and test in canary cluster in ~45 mins.

alice oncall: Proceed with rollback canary after we confirm fallback holds. Ben, coordinate with Erin for canary roll and automated health checks. Ops, keep draining dp-87f3 until we validate.

ben sres: Starting canary rollback to v1.4.2 on canary-taskset. Commands: ```./deployctl canary --service runtime --image runtime:v1.4.2 --checks 300s```

ops-bot: canary deploy started for runtime -> runtime:v1.4.2

ben sres: Canary healthy at 2m, runtime metrics look good, no CUDA OOMs on canary. Proceeding to staged rollout with automatic monitoring gating.

ops-bot: staged rollout -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% (gates passed)

ops-bot: runtime version runtime:v1.4.2 is now active in eu-north-1 for customer traffic (except dp-87f3 which is draining)

ben sres: After full rollback, we can attempt to bring NordicBank back from fallback to dedicated. Recommendation: redeploy dp-87f3 workers with runtime:v1.4.2 and run soak for 30m behind a rate limit.

alice oncall: ETA for re-route to dedicated?

ben sres: Redeploying dp-87f3 now: ```./infractl pool recreate --id dp-87f3 --image runtime:v1.4.2 --nodes 4``` Should be ready in ~18m.

ops-bot: pool dp-87f3 state changed -> RECREATING

ops-bot: pool dp-87f3 state changed -> ACTIVE (ready nodes=4)

ben sres: Pool back up. Running soak tests and synthetic traffic (sanitized). All green at 15m. Gradually shifting 25% traffic back and monitoring.

ben sres: Metrics: errors on dedicated endpoint back to baseline (0.3%), p95 latency normalized. No new OOMs.

carla acct-mgr: NordicBank execs on bridge. Provided the short timeline + we've proposed a 10% billing credit for this incident and a free week of premium support. They requested formal RCA doc and an exec one-pager.

frank security: Final note: continue to preserve crash dumps and network captures for 90 days. Flag for audit. No evidence of compromise.

alice oncall: Closing bridge in 5. Owners: Ben/Erin to draft RCA, Carla to draft exec note and coordinate credits + follow-up remediation timeline to customer, Frank to sign off on security statement, and me to file postmortem in /incidents/postmortems.

carla acct-mgr: I'll circulate the customer exec update and credit proposal within 30m. Also setting up a follow-up on next week's roadmap to discuss hardened tenant isolation options.

ben sres: RCA draft notes (for the postmortem doc): cause: quant kernel regression under extreme seq lengths -> CUDA OOM -> worker restarts -> cascading failures in dedicated pool; mitigations: tenant rate limit, fallback routing, kernel rollback; long-term: kv-eviction, better DRM for huge sequences, add tenant-level circuit breakers, and integration test for >10k seqs.

erin eng-runtime: I'll create a PR for the kv-eviction RFC and schedule the integration test job. Also will add a canary alert specifically for CUDA OOM rates per pool.

alice oncall: Thanks team. Filing thread/notes into the incident doc. Closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:
